newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China 1997 corn crop seen at 130 million tonnes.
newsitem.headline: China 1997 corn crop seen at 130 million tonnes.

text.p: China's corn output is seen rising by about 2.5 million tonnes this year over 1996 to reach 130 million tonnes, due to the planting of new hybrid crops and higher fertiliser use, a Chinese researcher said on Thursday. "This year's corn production will be good and the yield will increase to take the total production to 130 million tonnes," Kai mian Li, a researcher at the state-run Chinese Academy of Tropical and Agricultural Sciences in Hainan told Reuters.
The Statistical Bureau of the province of Guangdong reported China's corn output in 1996 at 127.47 million tonnes.
"The corn planting area will drop this year, because the 1996 area was simply too large," he said at the Asia Grain Markets '97 conference in Singapore.
Li said the reduced planted area would not affect total production as increased use of fertiliser and new cultivation methods will provide better yields in 1997.

He said a new high-yield type of corn, created by genetically engineering a wheat gene into corn to boost the protein level, could be introduced for the summer and autumn 1997 crop plantings, but declined to give further details.
Li put China's total area planted to corn in 1996 at 24.498 million hectares compared with 1995's 22.772 million, in a paper presented at the conference.
He said China will stop extending the area planted to corn, while increasing yields, to boost total production by about two percent by the year 2000 compared with 1996.
Li said the expansion in the planted area in 1996 stemmed from the good profits farmers made in 1994 and 1995 when corn prices were as high as 1,800 yuan a tonne.
Since late 1996, China has resumed corn exports due to last year's bumper crop and falling domestic prices.
"Traders want to export their corn as they have too much stock on hand while facing falling local prices," Li said.
China's corn exports soared to 1.09 million tonnes in the five months of this year. Domestic corn prices are currently at about 1,100 yuan a tonne.
Li warned, however, traders may have oversold corn and could be forced to buy back from the world market at the end of 1997.
China's demand for corn will continue to increase and it will need to maintain a total output of 124.3 million tonnes a year up to 2000 to cover its consumption, he said.

Li estimated that China's feed grain consumption will account for 40 percent of the country's total grain production by the year 2000 and reach 50 percent by 2030, due to increases in poultry and other livestock production.
